Torah #217 contains exactly one bechina declaration — 'הַלּוּחוֹת הֵם בְּחִינַת וָאו' — and this equation is already fully captured in the dataset as edge id 180.0 (node1_id: 'הלוחות', node2_id: 'אות וא"ו', reference: 217, type: 'bechina'). The single bechina edge yields one connected component of 2 nodes, which is the single existing package (torah_217_packages.json, Package 1: הַלּוּחוֹת וָאו). No new bechina edges were identified in the source text beyond what is already in the dataset. No new packages need to be created.

The teaching is structurally simple: one bechina identity (Tablets = vav) serves as the explanatory foundation for two acrostic observations (both phrases spelling Tammuz with missing vav). All other conceptual content in the Torah is eitza (causal) rather than bechina (parallel-nature) in character:

1. שְׁבִירַת הַלּוּחוֹת → שִׁכְחָה: The breaking of the Tablets caused forgetting. Pure eitza.
2. שְׁבִירַת הַלּוּחוֹת → נִסְתַּלֵּק הַוָּאו: The breaking caused the removal of the vav from the word Tammuz. Pure eitza.
3. הַמְשָׁכַת זִכָּרוֹן בְּתַמּוּז → תִּקּוּן הַשִּׁכְחָה: Drawing down memory in Tammuz repairs the forgetting. The practical prescription. Pure eitza.

The absence of new package proposals reflects the Torah's intentional minimalism: it is a structural insight — one bechina, two acrostics, one causal chain — rather than a multi-layered conceptual teaching with numerous parallel identifications.
